title: Model Delivery, Multimodal Pipelines, and Offline Governance

scout.purpose: Master model delivery, multimodal pipelines, and offline governance through a production or platform contract supported by causal evidence.
scout.realWorldUse: Specialist Android work must remain compatible, secure, measurable, accessible, distributable, and operable outside a demonstration.
scout.outcome: You can design, inspect, test, release, and defend model delivery, multimodal pipelines, and offline governance.

blocks.text: Bundling a model guarantees first-run offline availability but increases app download and couples updates to releases. On-demand delivery reduces initial size and allows model updates, but requires network, storage, integrity, compatibility, progress, retry, eviction, and rollback. Define a minimum bundled capability or honest unavailable state. Verify digest or signature before activation, write atomically, keep the last known-good model, and bind model version to preprocessing, labels, runtime, thresholds, and feature configuration.

blocks.text: A multimodal pipeline composes camera, audio, text, sensors, retrieval, and one or more models. Each boundary changes format, timestamp, coordinate space, confidence, privacy, and cancellation. Synchronize by stable input identity and discard late output. Never concatenate sensitive modalities into logs or analytics. Apply data minimization before inference, isolate temporary files, and state whether processing is local, remote, or hybrid. Generated output needs uncertainty UX, safety filters, human correction, and accessible alternatives.

blocks.caption: A focused fragment whose complete contract includes exact versions, ownership, adverse paths, compatibility, and release evidence.

blocks.text: Stage model exposure independently but preserve server and client compatibility. Monitor download success, activation, fallback, latency, quality proxy, resource cost, and opt-out without raw content. Test interrupted download, corruption, downgrade, disk full, runtime mismatch, offline launch, clock change, process death, and rollback. A model kill switch must retain user data and provide meaningful degraded behavior. Govern training and evaluation sources, licenses, bias, deletion, incident response, and model retirement.

Expert engineering makes assumptions, authority, compatibility, security, privacy, accessibility, performance, distribution, and recovery reviewable. Begin with a concrete user or platform outcome, identify trust and lifecycle boundaries, and retain exact source, dependency, toolchain, configuration, model or platform version, and artifact identity. Test realistic success plus denial, offline, process death, cancellation, corruption, version skew, resource pressure, and dependency failure. Measure representative distributions rather than best runs. Document unsupported cases, residual risk, owners, release gates, incident response, deprecation, and rollback or roll-forward. A specialised solution is production-ready only when another team can integrate, verify, operate, upgrade, disable, and remove it safely.

blocks.title: Expert trap
blocks.text: Watch carefully for this common failure mode in production: Replacing the active model file in place can leave a corrupt partial model after process death or storage failure.

inspect.title: Inspect Model Delivery, Multimodal Pipelines, and Offline Governance
walkthrough: Identify the user or platform outcome, authority, lifecycle, supported versions, and exact artifact context.
Trace data, execution, security, compatibility, delivery, and failure ownership across every boundary.
Verify representative evidence, adverse paths, release gates, support, migration, and safe recovery.
inspect.expectedOutput: A reproducible expert artifact or investigation with explicit contracts, limitations, evidence, and operational ownership.

trap_check.mistake: Replacing the active model file in place can leave a corrupt partial model after process death or storage failure.
trap_check.why: It hides an ownership, compatibility, trust, lifecycle, or evidence gap that becomes costly outside the demonstration.
trap_check.fix: Make the disputed boundary explicit and add a representative negative or compatibility test plus operational response.

trap_check.mistake: Treating one successful device, client, model, platform build, or release as proof of the supported contract.
trap_check.why: Advanced Android ecosystems contain version, hardware, consumer, policy, and runtime variation.
trap_check.fix: Define the support matrix and verify exact artifacts across representative and adverse conditions.

challenge_intro.task: Design a signed on-demand multimodal model rollout with offline baseline, atomic activation, compatibility, privacy, staged metrics, kill switch, and rollback.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: The work includes a minimal coherent implementation, exact evidence, support and threat boundaries, adverse testing, release operation, and recovery.

recall.prompt: Why retain a last known-good model?
recall.answer: A failed, incompatible, or harmful download can be deactivated without removing the user’s existing offline capability.

recall.prompt: What must accompany an expert Android artifact?
recall.answer: Exact source and build identity, supported versions, contracts, tests, measurements, security and privacy review, release evidence, owner, and recovery plan.
They prevent consumers and operators from treating an untested or impossible condition as a silent guarantee.
